title: Jewel Toned French Carrot Confit
description: A traditional French dish from Normandy featuring carrots cooked in salted butter, this confit is perfect for a lazy Sunday, with a twist of fermentation for added depth of flavor. The result is a deliciously crisp and savory side dish.

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.notes: peeled and sliced into 1/4 inch thick rounds

instructions: In a large bowl, combine the sliced carrots and granulated sugar, letting it sit for 30 minutes to allow the carrots to release their moisture.
Rinse the carrots and set them aside, then in a large saucepan, melt the salted butter over medium heat.
Add the apple cider vinegar, water, thyme, bay leaves, black pepper, and sea salt to the saucepan, stirring to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and add the sliced carrots to the saucepan.
Simmer the carrots for 20 minutes, or until they are tender and caramelized.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and let it cool to room temperature.
Cover the saucepan with plastic wrap and refrigerate it for at least 24 hours to allow the carrots to ferment.
Before serving, bring the confit to room temperature and serve the carrots crispy, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
